newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Exsa studies $150 mln ammonium plants.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Exsa studies $150 mln ammonium plants.

text.p: Exsa S.A., Peru's largest explosives manufacturer, is studying an investment plan to invest $150 million in the construction of an ammonium nitrate plant and an ammoniac plant, a company official said Thursday.

Exsa hopes to find a partner for the project in the first quarter next year and is negotiating with firms from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Spain, company spokesman Karl Maslo said in an interview.
He named only France's Grande Paroisse, which is controlled by the oil giant Elf Aquitaine, as one of the companies talking to Exsa about the plants.

The ammonium nitrate plant, which would have a production capacity of between 150,000 and 180,000 tonnes a year, would cost $100 million, while the ammoniac plant would cost $50 million, Maslo said without giving details of the second plant's capacity.
The company has not fixed a goal for the start-up of the plants.

Exsa wants to build the two plants to meet Peru's growing ammonium demand, which is seen rising to 137,000 tonnes a year in 2000 and 220,000 tonnes a year by 2010 from a current 83,000 tonnes a year, Maslo said.
This increased demand will be driven by a growing mining sector that currently accounts for around half of the country's total ammonium needs, the Exsa official added.
The Exsa plants would use gas from the huge Camisea reserves, if, as expected, a consortium of Royal Dutch/Shell and Mobil exploit the fields and transport their gas to Lima, he added.
